justifications.c1: Replacement cost figures ($2,950-$12,000) come only from US vendor guides with unconfirmed per-page attribution; researcher found no UK price and no figure for life lost to under-watering.
justifications.c2: Watering at each charge / weekly is stated by Hoppecke UK, BHS and Redway (all battery or watering vendors) plus a non-UK hire contract requiring daily checks; no statistic on under-watering events.
justifications.c3: Paid battery service plans with monthly visits and fixed monthly pricing (Exide, search-confirmed), Hoppecke and Crown UK contracts; no price per visit or in-house labour quantified; all sources sell the service.
justifications.c4: No statutory duty; contractual pressure only: a US warranty requiring maintenance records (Scribd, attribution unverified), German/other non-UK hire T&Cs, and FLTA fair-wear guidance (search-confirmed).
justifications.c5: No MHE/fleet manager job adverts searched; the buyer (3PL vs battery service manager) is inferred from Exide's monthly pricing line.
justifications.c6: Battery makers' service arms (Exide, Hoppecke) and OEM dealers (Crown UK) visit sites monthly and EnerSys sells Wi-iQ monitoring, so channels selling adjacent technology exist, though they are also competitors.
justifications.c7: EnerSys Wi-iQ5 (electrolyte detection, LTE/BLE) and Philadelphia Scientific Blinky family (UL Classified, ~$48, search-confirmed) cover the need; lithium-ion is forecast to overtake lead-acid around 2026, shrinking the base.
justifications.c8: Pilot-cell electrolyte sensing and combined current/level monitoring are proven (Blinky, Wi-iQ), but no component prices and hydrogen/ATEX in charging rooms was not checked.
justifications.c9: Exide sells service at a fixed monthly price and fair-wear disputes recur at off-hire, but no comparable monitoring subscription price and a declining lead-acid fleet.
justifications.c10: FLTA fair-wear warnings in trade press (Forkliftaction, Logistics Matters), a 2006 TCC case that is not about watering, and a vendor warning (Hoppecke); no forum complaints or enforcement data.

weakest: The addressable lead-acid base is shrinking as lithium-ion overtakes it, and strong incumbents (EnerSys Wi-iQ, Blinky) already cover electrolyte monitoring.
